correctness.rationale: The sum of vertical increments over a primitive two-cycle is c(x0+x1)=0. Because c≠0, x1=−x0; x0=0 would imply a fixed point. Thus the two horizontal multipliers are both −1, forcing a=−2(1+y0²)=−2(1+y1²). The ordinates differ by cx0≠0, so they are exactly u and −u with u>0, and the horizontal coordinates follow. Reversal of sign merely exchanges the two points. Direct substitution gives existence for all a<−2 and the equality endpoint gives no primitive cycle. At both points xy=−2u²/c; the derivative is the same trace-zero matrix with entries (−1, −8u²/[c(1+u²)]; c, 1). Its square is minus its determinant times the identity, i.e. (1−7u²)/(1+u²) I. This gives the sink/source windows and the repeated −1 endpoint. At a=−16/7 the return derivative is the zero operator, not merely a matrix with two zero eigenvalues. Since the return is smooth on the plane, at each point the return error obeys a local O(norm(error)²) bound and hence converges for sufficiently small initial errors. No nonlinear classification follows at the repeated −1 endpoint.
